question.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthonormal?

I. $U=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\}$

II. $V=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\}$

III. $W=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}]\}$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
$\{{u}_{1},{u}_{2},{u}_{3}\},$ 
$\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\},$ and 
$\{{w}_{1},{w}_{2}\},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthonormal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- $\{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0 \\ {u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{3}=0 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{3}=0\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1}=1 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{2}=1 \\ {u}_{3}\cdot {u}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}=1 \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}$

- $\{\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0 \\ {w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{3}=0 \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{3}=0\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,\{\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1}=1 \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2}=1 \\ {w}_{3}\cdot {w}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=1+25+4=30\ne 1 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $U$ is not an orthonormal set.

- For the set $V,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]=-\frac{6}{13}+\frac{6}{13}=0 & ✓ \\ {v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{4}{13}+\frac{9}{13}=1 & ✓ \\ {v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{9}{13}+\frac{4}{13}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $V$ is orthonormal.

- For the set $W,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{18}}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{18}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{18}}=0 & ✓ \\ {w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{6}+\frac{4}{6}+\frac{1}{6}=1 & ✓ \\ {w}_{2}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=1 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $W$ is orthonormal.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$V$ and $W$ only".
